title: Clipbasket for Omarchy settings
description: The settings contract for Clipbasket on Omarchy. Persisted to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/clipbasket/settings.json (default ~/.config/clipbasket/settings.json). Seed it with `clipbasket-omarchy settings-init`, which derives the defaults below so they live in exactly one place. Any key absent from the file falls back to its default here; unknown keys are preserved untouched so a downgrade never destroys a newer install's settings.

notInThisPort.name: theme
notInThisPort.reason: Omarchy owns theming. The panel is built from Omarchy's own Style tokens and follows the active theme; an app-level override would fight it.

notInThisPort.name: automaticallyCheckForUpdates
notInThisPort.reason: git and pacman own updates here. `git -C ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/clipbasket.clipboard pull` is the update mechanism; there is nothing for the app to check.

notInThisPort.name: pastePermission (macOS Accessibility)
notInThisPort.reason: Wayland has no equivalent grant. Synthetic input goes through wtype/ydotool, which either work or are not installed.

notInThisPort.name: openAtCursorOnShortcut
notInThisPort.reason: Nothing could consume it. The popup is a layer-shell surface anchored to the bar pill by Omarchy’s own Panel chrome, which positions it relative to the widget rather than the pointer; there is no supported way for the plugin to place it at the cursor, so the setting only ever described an intention.

notInThisPort.name: launchAtLogin
notInThisPort.reason: The shell starts capture; there is nothing to opt out of. Service.qml owns the wl-paste watchers, so capture runs exactly when omarchy-shell runs, and dies with it. The setting was inert even before that: nothing read the key it wrote.

notInThisPort.name: closePanelAfterCopy
notInThisPort.reason: The macOS app kept this in lockstep with closePanelAfterSelection through the UI. Collapsed into the single closePanelAfterAction.

validation.message: Auto-paste requires closing the popup first.
validation.note: Ported verbatim from the macOS app's normalize_settings: pasting into the focused window while the panel still holds focus pastes into the panel.

globalShortcut.title: Global shortcut
globalShortcut.description: The key that opens Clipbasket. The compositor owns this on Wayland — change it in ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua, or run `clipbasket-omarchy make-default`.

x-clipbasket.help: Display-only mirror of the managed block in bindings.lua, written by `clipbasket-omarchy make-default` and cleared by `restore-default`. The panel must render it but must never write it: writing here would desynchronise the file that actually decides the binding. It defaults to empty because a fresh install deliberately does not take a key — Omarchy's own clipboard keeps SUPER + CTRL + V until the user asks otherwise.
x-clipbasket.source: ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua, between the `-- >>> clipbasket` and `-- <<< clipbasket` markers
x-clipbasket.unboundLabel: Not bound — Omarchy's clipboard owns SUPER + CTRL + V

maxClips.title: Maximum saved clips
maxClips.description: Most users copy 20-50 items a day. 500 clips is about two weeks, 1000 about a month, 2000 about two months.

x-clipbasket.help: Values outside the range are clamped rather than rejected, matching the macOS app. Pinned and saved clips are exempt from the prune.

ignoreConfidentialCopies.title: Ignore confidential copies
ignoreConfidentialCopies.description: Never record items marked concealed, like passwords copied from password managers.

x-clipbasket.help: On Wayland this means skipping offers carrying the x-kde-passwordManagerHint MIME type, and copies made while CLIPBOARD_STATE=sensitive. Defaults on: a privacy default should never need to be discovered.

closePanelAfterAction.title: Close popup after action
closePanelAfterAction.description: Hide the popup after selecting or copying a clip.

x-clipbasket.help: Turning this off disables auto-paste, which cannot work while the panel still holds focus.

pasteSelectedClipImmediately.title: Paste immediately
pasteSelectedClipImmediately.description: After picking a clip, paste it into the focused window instead of only copying it.

x-clipbasket.help: Wayland has no system-wide synthetic-input API, so this shells out to wtype (or ydotool with a running daemon). The panel should present it as unavailable, not merely off, when neither is installed.
x-clipbasket.unavailableLabel: Install wtype to enable automatic paste
